<span id="一-概述"></span>
# 1. Overview

**Mutual exclusion domain**, also known as mutual exclusion domain, mutual exclusion layer, experimental layer.

**Mutual exclusion experiments**, that is, experiments in **different mutual exclusion domains**. The traffic between mutual exclusion experiments is mutual exclusion. If a user hits Experiment 1 in the mutual exclusion domain, it will not hit the experiments corresponding to other mutual exclusion domains in the mutual exclusion domain group, but will still be orthogonal to other experiments in the same mutual exclusion domain.

**Basic principles:** 


1. **Experiments with the same or related content that may affect each other are recommended to be added to different mutual exclusion domains in the same mutual exclusion domain group.**  For example, if you want to experiment with button color and button shape at the same time, you need to add two experiments to different mutual exclusion domains in the same mutual exclusion domain group.

2. **Experiments that are not related to each other can be created in different mutual exclusion domain groups to reuse traffic.**  For example, if you want to experiment with an algorithm and a button color at the same time, you can create two experiments in different mutual exclusion domain groups.


<span id="二-为什么需要互斥组？"></span>
# 2. Why do we need mutual exclusion domain?

Mutual exclusion domain technology is a traffic layering technology developed to enable multiple experiments to be parallel and not interfere with each other, and to obtain enough traffic. Mutual exclusion domain technology can "copy" the overall traffic countless times, forming countless mutual exclusion domains, so that the overall traffic can be reused countless times, thereby improving experimental efficiency.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/884319636aa349379d3793a605118845~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


* Experimental traffic in **the same mutual exclusion domain group in different mutual exclusion domains** is **mutual exclusion**, for example, creating a mutual exclusion domain group of e\-commerce businesses, which plans two mutual exclusion domains: iterative domain and blank domain, the experimental traffic of these two mutual exclusion domains is mutual exclusion.

* Traffic in **different mutual exclusion domain groups or the same mutual exclusion domain** is **orthogonal**, such as e\-commerce business experiment and social business experiment. It can be simply understood as: under the premise that the mutual exclusion domain is selected correctly, the traffic is scientifically distributed to ensure that the results of each experiment will not be disturbed by experiments in other mutual exclusion domains. If you want to learn more about "orthogonal", read the next paragraph or skip it.


<span id="可选读-什么是正交？"></span>
## (Optional reading) What is orthogonal?

As mentioned above, traffic within different mutual exclusion domain groups or the same mutual exclusion domain is orthogonal. How to understand traffic "orthogonal"? What is orthogonal for?

Let me give you an example. Let's say there are two experiments. Experiment A (experimental group labeled A1, control group labeled A2) was distributed in mutual exclusion domain group1 and took 100% of the traffic; Experiment B (experimental group labeled B1, control group labeled B2) was distributed in mutual exclusion domain group2 and also took 100% of the traffic. (Note that mutual exclusion domain group1 and mutual exclusion domain group2 are actually the same batch of traffic, and mutual exclusion domain group2 replicates the traffic of mutual exclusion domain group1.)

If the two mutual exclusion domain groups are not processed, let the A1 group and the B1 group get the same traffic, and the A2 group and the B2 group get the same traffic (as shown below). This means that when a user is hit by group A1, he or she will also be hit by group B1. Then, the experimental strategies of both experiments were demonstrated to the user.

After a period of experimentation, we found that the data of experimental group B1 increased. At this point, we need to ask a question: **B1 group's metrics increased, is B1's strategy effective?**  **Could it be affected by the A1 group policy?** 

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

Judging from the current distribution of traffic, we cannot answer this question. The index of group B1 has increased, which may or may not be influenced by group A1. So how should we distribute traffic to confirm whether the metric of group B1 is increasing and has nothing to do with group A1?

The answer is to make the traffic "**orthogonal**".

If you divide the traffic of group A1 into two halves, one into group B1 and one into group B2, then divide the traffic of group A2 into two halves, one into group B1 and one into group B2. Then the traffic for the two experiments will be as shown in the figure below. At this point, between Experiment A and Experiment B, a **traffic "orthogonal" is formed**.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

It can be found that, because half of the traffic in group A1 is in B1 and the other half is in B2, even if A1's policy has an impact on experiment B, the impact is evenly distributed between the two groups of experiment B. In this case, if the metric of group B1 increases, then it can be ruled out that B1 is influenced by A1 to form an increase. This is the meaning of traffic orthogonality.

The web\-traffic splitting service of BytePlus A/B testing goes through two operations of the "hash function", so that the traffic between different mutual exclusion domains is orthogonal. **In the case of orthogonal traffic, experiments in different mutual exclusion domains are uniformly dispersed, making the experimental index results more trustworthy.** 

<span id="c294ff82"></span>
# 3. Functional limitations


* The current DataTester provides you with the ability to "group by mutual exclusion domain", supporting multi\-layer nested mutual exclusion domains. This function is a value\-added function. If you wish to use it, you need to purchase it separately. For details, please contact BytePlus technical support staff or customer manager.

* When using the mutual exclusion domain feature:

   * Server side SDK: Only Java and Go type server side SDKs support the use of mutual exclusion domains, and Java SDKs need to be 2.0.19 and above, and Go SDKs need to be 1.0.6 and above.

   * Client side SDK: The mutual exclusion domain feature is available in all versions of the client side SDK.


<span id="三-应用场景"></span>
# 4. Application scenario


* If the experimental traffic is not enough, but you want to do multiple experiments and don't want to waste time, you can add a mutual exclusion domain group to the experiment to solve the problem of insufficient experimental traffic.

* If you need to conduct two experiments at the same time (e.g. button color & button shape), but conducting the experiments together will affect the experimental results, then you need to add these two experiments to different mutual exclusion domains in a mutual exclusion domain group.

* Traffic layer list

The actionable content is as follows:


* **Search:**  You can enter mutual exclusion domain ID, name, description to search.

* **Create:**  Click "Create mutual exclusion domain group" and "Create traffic layer" to create a new one.

* **Number of experiments:**  You can see which experiments are being used and current traffic usage.

* **Modify:**  You can modify the mutual exclusion domain name (unique to the same application mutual exclusion domain name), mutual exclusion domain description, and experimental type.

* **Delete:**  When the number of experiments is 0, the traffic layer can be deleted; when there is no bound traffic layer in the mutual exclusion domain, the mutual exclusion domain can be deleted.

# 6. Create traffic layer, mutual exclusion domain

<span id="b6fce75b"></span>
## Create traffic layer

On the traffic layer list page, click "Create Traffic Layer" and configure the traffic layer parameters in the pop\-up sidebar page to create a traffic layer.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/b63bf2d4364d4b7fbc28bdef132f556e~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

<span id="a5ce0733"></span>
## Create a new mutual exclusion domain and bind the traffic layer

On the mutual exclusion domain list page, click "Create mutual exclusion domain" to pop up the mutual exclusion domain creation page. As shown below:

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/4eddeb5dcf5f4feb9dd0cb77ad19e62d~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


* Fill in the group name and experiment type.

* You can safely turn on the switch for nested child mutual exclusion domain groups to bind child mutual exclusion domains for mutual exclusion domains. You can choose a mutual exclusion domain that has been created as a child mutual exclusion domain, or directly create a new mutual exclusion domain as a child mutual exclusion domain.

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">warning   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">When you select a mutual exclusion domain that has been created by binding as a child mutual exclusion domain, binding an associated mutual exclusion domain is not supported.   </div>
   

* To bind a traffic layer for a mutual exclusion domain, you can select a traffic layer that has already been created, or create a new one directly.

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">warning   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">When selecting to bind the traffic layer that has been created, it is not supported to bind the traffic layer that has been associated with the experiment to avoid directly affecting the existing experiment.   </div>
   

<span id="六-使用互斥组"></span>
# 7. Using mutual exclusion domains

Taking the programming experiment as an example, in the second step of creating the experiment, "Set the effective policy", the traffic layer that has been created can be selected in the experimental layer. If the facility traffic is mutual exclusion, the created mutual exclusion domain can be selected. As shown below:

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/a4e807cd70df4118b426392a2eedf5e8~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

**To add a mutual exclusion domain to an experiment, the basic rules are as follows:** 


* Client side experiments can only add client side mutual exclusion domains, and server side experiments can only add server side mutual exclusion domains.

* Draft box and debugging experiments support for adding mutual exclusion domains. Running experiments support adding mutual exclusion domains that do not have running experiments, but mutual exclusion domains that already have running experiments cannot be added.

* If a running experiment already exists in a mutual exclusion domain, other running experiments cannot be added to the mutual exclusion domain, but experiments in the draft box and debugging can be added to the mutual exclusion domain.


**To remove a mutual exclusion domain for an experiment, the basic rules are as follows:** 


* Draft box and debugging experiments support for removing mutual exclusion domains. Running experiments do not support removing mutual exclusion domains.


**Permission related:**  All mutual exclusion domains are public mutual exclusion domains, and any user in the current application of the group has the permission to "create a mutual exclusion domain, view a mutual exclusion domain, modify a mutual exclusion domain, and log off a mutual exclusion domain".
